summary: Design gender-sensitive resilience programmes using GIS, climate data, markets, and adaptive social protection. Build practical outputs with TrainingCred.
lede: Climate-resilient agriculture and adaptive social protection design links climate risks to livelihood support. It is for professionals who plan, coordinate, finance, monitor, or improve resilience programmes and need to turn climate and livelihood evidence into practical interventions. Participants practise climate hazard screening and GIS exposure mapping, gender-responsive targeting, and selecting adaptive support such as cash transfers, public works, or livelihood grants.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who design, coordinate, finance, monitor, or improve climate and agriculture resilience interventions. It is especially relevant when you must connect climate evidence with agricultural livelihoods, gender inclusion, local markets, and social protection delivery.
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in programme design, agricultural extension, social protection planning, humanitarian response, donor project management, MEAL, or related resilience work. Prior GIS experience helps but is not required. No coding or programming is required for completion. The course teaches climate analytics and AI-assisted geospatial workflows at an operational application level, while advanced climate modelling and production software development remain conceptual.
